title: Cohesion and coupling
idea: High cohesion means a class's members all serve one purpose; low coupling means it knows as little as possible about other classes.

analogy.text: In a good kitchen each station keeps its own tools. Waiters pass orders through the hatch; they never open the chef's fridge.
analogy.breaks: Cooks can improvise; classes only honour the methods they publish.

points: Cohesion asks: do this class's fields and methods change for the same reason?
Coupling asks: how many other classes break when this one changes inside?
Ask an object a question; never reach into its internals and do its maths.
In interviews, justify each class by naming its one job and its few collaborators.

hero.title: A promo reaching into the cart

steps.caption: `PromoEngine` gets the cart's internal list and filters it in place. It now depends on how `Cart` stores items.
It also reads each `Item` price itself. Pricing maths that belongs to the cart now lives outside it.
The receipt page asks `Cart` for its total. The promo deleted the sticker, so the total silently drops to 4000.
Raise cohesion: `Cart` owns its items and every calculation over them. Its getter returns a copy.
Lower coupling: the promo asks `Cart` one question and never sees a `List` or an `Item`.
The receipt and the promo now share only the `Cart` methods. Changing storage inside `Cart` breaks neither.

code.title: The problem
code.caption: The promo reaches into the cart and edits its list. Compare the totals before and after.

walk.text: `items()` returns the live list, so every caller is coupled to the cart's storage.
The promo filters that list in place to find eligible items. It mutates someone else's state.
The discount maths sits outside `Cart`, although it uses only the cart's data: low cohesion.
The discount is right, but the cart lost an item. The bug shows up far from its cause.

code.title: The fix
code.caption: `Cart` answers questions about its own items; the promo depends on one method and an interface.

walk.text: `Item` validates itself, so no other class has to check prices.
Items are private and the getter returns `List.copyOf`. Outsiders cannot edit the cart.
Both totals use one method over the cart's own data. That is high cohesion.
`Promo` is a narrow contract. New promos plug in without touching `Cart`.
The promo asks one question and does one division. It knows nothing about storage.
The cart is unchanged after the promo runs. Each class owns its own effects.

pitfalls: Getters returning live collections let any caller corrupt state; return `List.copyOf` or an unmodifiable view.
Long chains like `a.getB().getC().getD()` couple you to three classes; ask the first one instead.
A `Utils` or `Manager` class with unrelated methods has low cohesion; every team edits it.

quiz.q: A `ReportService` reads `order.getCustomer().getAddress().getCountry()` to pick a tax rate. What is the best change?
options: Make Address fields public to skip the getters
Add order.taxCountry() and let Order answer it
Copy the country into ReportService at startup
Make ReportService extend Order to reach the fields
quiz.why: `Order` already holds the path to the country, so it should answer. `ReportService` then depends on one method, not on `Customer` and `Address` too.

takeaway: Keep related work together; let classes ask, not reach in.

starters: How do I measure coupling in a class I already have?
